name: Insurance and Jobsite Risk Controls
headline: Insurance and Jobsite Risk Controls
articleBody: Before hiring, homeowners should confirm workers’ compensation coverage, general liability insurance, and a clear policy for damage caused during construction. California contractor guidance and industry risk-management practice both emphasize that insurance is not a formality; it is a practical protection if a worker is injured, a pipe leaks, or material damage occurs during demolition. The contractor should be able to name the insurer and provide current certificates, and the documents should match the contracting entity named on the agreement. If subcontractors are used, homeowners should ask whether those subcontractors are covered and whether the general contractor verifies coverage before work starts. Kitchen projects create elevated risk because water, gas, electric, and sharp tools are all present at once, and a simple mistake can affect adjacent rooms, flooring, or even neighboring units in multi-family buildings. It is also sensible to ask how the contractor secures the jobsite, handles dust containment, and protects floors and access paths. Insurance does not replace careful workmanship, but it helps define what happens when an accident occurs. For Los Angeles County homeowners, this is especially important in occupied homes where work may proceed while the family remains on site.
